proposal.summary:
All three current winners keep their place on individual merit; none is beaten by a verified alternative on its own terms, but one pin is stale and the layer's deep gaps remain genuinely open pending a paid-entitlement decision outside this research task's scope.

alpaca-py (v0.44.0) is exactly current against both PyPI (upload_time 2026-08-11T10:15:07Z) and GitHub releases/latest (published 2026-08-11T10:11:55Z) -- confirmed by the incoming adversarial pass and independently reproducible. No free/open Python SDK substitutes for Alpaca's own API, and no rival (Massive, Databento, OpenBB) has an executed on-stack arm beating alpaca-py's measured 24,310,292-bar broad-universe acquisition (0 failed batches, 5,108 pages re-hashed, 0 mismatches; catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json trading[0]). The incoming packet's own adversarial check caught its own minor error (a pushed_at citation off by one calendar day); trivial, doesn't change the verdict.

exchange_calendars (4.13.2) is also exactly current; its 29 unreleased upstream commits, read in full, are dependency bumps, CI/lint and an AGENTS.md addition only -- no calendar-semantic change missed. New grounding this pass added: reading blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/sessions.py and runner.py directly shows exchange_calendars is wired into the live paper engine as an optional session-open fallback behind a primary hand-rolled session table, so this pick has a real (if secondary) effect on paper-lane session gating -- which raises the value of finally running the pandas_market_calendars comparison the layer's own decision text has deferred since at least 2026-09-23 ("should not be mixed" without one).

edgartools is the one winner that is stale, not challenged: its pin (v5.58.0, 2026-09-11) sits two releases behind upstream v5.59.1 (2026-09-26, independently reconfirmed today via gh api, exact timestamp match). Both missed releases are correctness fixes on exactly what this project uses the library for: v5.59.0 fixes seven 10-K/10-Q table-of-contents section-boundary bugs (an issuer's Item 7 wrongly returning Item 8 text); v5.59.1 fixes a same-day regression plus a bug where edgar_read returned zero 13F holdings for any filing, until hours before this review. No alternative filing library beats edgartools; the action is a pin bump to v5.59.1, not a swap.

The layer's hard, named gaps -- a survivorship-free universe, complete corporate actions (dividend currency), established historical point-in-time availability, and licensing/redistribution rights -- remain open, and every candidate that could plausibly close them is already known to this stack, not newly discovered today: Databento is already a "conditional" catalog card since at least 2026-09-22/23 (pin v0.86.0), and is itself now one release behind its own upstream v0.87.0 (released 2026-09-22, independently reconfirmed live today via pypi.org -- no further drift since the 0923 sweep, but the bump is still pending). Sharadar's only Python access path, the nasdaq-data-link wrapper, was already found code-stale in the 2026-09-23 sweep (no PyPI release since 1.0.4 on 2022-08-29; its 2026-09-15 repo push is an unmerged README branch, not a functional update) -- independently reconfirmed. Norgate was already logged as "not new" in a 2026-09-24 sweep, blocked on a paid subscription and an unread EULA; independently refetching norgatedata.com today confirms it is Windows-desktop-only with "access... no longer possible if a subscription lapses" -- in real tension with this layer's own "produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots" requirement. CRSP is reachable in this stack only via WRDS, already deeply reviewed under the identity-provenance layer, and blocked by WRDS's own terms restricting use to "academic and non-commercial research purposes only" -- a licensing wall, not a cost question. OpenBB was already source-reviewed at a pinned commit (authenticated-data-review.json) and deferred; independently reconfirmed today that GitHub's own license.spdx_id is NOASSERTION (not "AGPL-3.0-only" as the incoming packet characterized it) while the repo's own pinned LICENSE file text is AGPLv3 -- a correction, not a reversal, since either way it's an unresolved copyleft-flavored license plus a generic fetcher pipeline that doesn't enforce this project's raw-byte/provenance contract.

Given all of that, "add_candidates" is the honest disposition: not "keep" (a pin is genuinely stale and several trial-worthy comparisons have never been run), not "challenge" (no alternative has verified, executed evidence of beating any winner outright). This pass registers concrete, boundable trial plans for the pieces that are tractable without a purchase -- an edgartools pin bump, a pandas_market_calendars side-by-side now motivated by exchange_calendars' real paper-lane wiring, and a free-tier edgartools-v5.59.1-vs-sec-api-python 13F diff motivated by edgartools' own just-fixed bug -- plus a bounded, entitlement-gated Databento/Sharadar trial design for whenever the user separately authorizes that paid-data decision. The deepest gaps correctly stay open; no research candidate found today closes them for free.

winner_status.note: Pin v0.44.0 is exactly upstream's current latest (PyPI upload_time 2026-08-11T10:15:07Z; GitHub releases/latest v0.44.0 published 2026-08-11T10:11:55Z) -- confirmed by the incoming adversarial pass and reproduced independently. No free/open Python SDK substitutes for Alpaca's own market-data/brokerage API, and no rival (Massive, Databento, OpenBB) has an executed on-stack arm beating alpaca-py's measured 24,310,292-bar broad-universe acquisition recorded in the 2026-09-23 sweep. The incoming packet's own adversarial pass caught a minor self-error (pushed_at citation off by one calendar day, live value 2026-09-23T08:14:11Z not the claimed 2026-09-24); trivial, doesn't change the verdict.

Pin v5.58.0 (2026-09-11) is two releases behind upstream v5.59.1 (2026-09-26) -- independently reconfirmed today via gh api repos/dgunning/edgartools/releases/latest, exact match to the incoming packet. Both missed releases are correctness fixes on this project's actual filing-parsing use: v5.59.0 fixes seven 10-K/10-Q table-of-contents section-boundary bugs; v5.59.1 fixes a same-day regression plus a bug where edgar_read returned zero 13F holdings for any filing, until today. No alternative filing-parser beats edgartools on evidence (sec-api-python is broader-scope and paid, not a free substitute) -- recommended action is a pin bump to v5.59.1, not a swap.

Pin 4.13.2 is exactly upstream's latest tag; its 29 unreleased upstream commits, read in full, are dependency bumps, CI/lint and an AGENTS.md addition only -- no calendar-semantic change missed (independently reconfirmed via the same compare API). New grounding this pass added: blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/sessions.py and runner.py import exchange_calendars as a live (optional, fallback) session-open cross-check behind the paper engine's primary session table, so this pick has a real, if secondary, effect on paper-lane session gating. A genuine, actively maintained, permissively licensed comparator (pandas_market_calendars) exists but has never been run side by side on this repo's own sessions; earns_it stands per the layer's own overturn_when gate (compare before switching), with that comparison now better motivated and listed as a challenger.

challengers.name: Databento (databento-python SDK + dbn status schema + corporate-actions/reference-data + security master)
challengers.why_better: The only externally verified candidate that plausibly addresses three named gaps at once: corporate-action completeness (an explicit, dated event taxonomy on Databento's own docs/blog), historical halt/LULD reconstruction via its normalized `status` schema (cross-checked against the primary Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH 5.0 specification text itself, not just vendor marketing, per catalogs/us-equities/mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json), and a security master claiming 310,000+ listed/delisted securities across 85,000+ issuers -- a figure independently repeated across four separate research passes on 2026-09-22, 09-23, 09-24 and today, though every pass agrees it remains a vendor claim never checked against this project's own retained symbol list. Already an existing 'conditional' catalog card (data-databento), so this is a maturation of a known candidate, not a new find.
challengers.trial_plan: (1) Zero-cost first step: bump the already-approved conditional card's SDK pin from v0.86.0 to v0.87.0 (released 2026-09-22, independently reconfirmed live via pypi.org today -- still current, no further drift since the 2026-09-23 sweep flagged it pin_behind_upstream). (2) If and only if the user separately authorizes a paid Databento entitlement (out of scope for this research-only task), extend the existing blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/compare.py-style harness with a Databento arm on the same frozen AAPL/SPY window alpaca-py already covers, adding at least one symbol delisted within that window (which the current AAPL-only sample never exercises). Pass criterion: Databento returns bar/corporate-action records for the delisted symbol that alpaca-py's feed cannot, and a fixed as-of pull reproduces byte-identical corporate-action records on repeat. Overturn: if the entitled trial shows no material coverage difference for the project's actual retained universe, or measured cost is unacceptable, keep alpaca-py as sole default and downgrade the Databento card.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none (research/backtest data-completeness question; no execution path in the adaptive-paper engine currently reads from Databento)

challengers.name: Sharadar SEP/SF1 (data itself, accessed directly -- not via the nasdaq-data-link PyPI wrapper)
challengers.why_better: Sharadar's own docs (fetched 2026-09-26) quote an explicit as-reported/point-in-time dimension (ARQ/ARY/ART) that excludes restatements and is time-indexed to the actual filing submission date -- a direct, quotable answer to this layer's 'reject data whose historical availability... is unknown' clause for fundamentals specifically, plus SEP's corporate-actions/reference coverage back to 1998 for 21,000+ active and delisted tickers. The only Python client (nasdaq-data-link, formerly Quandl) is independently confirmed code-stale: no PyPI release since 1.0.4 on 2022-08-29, and its most recent repo push (2026-09-15) is an unmerged README branch, not a functional update (catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json adversarial lens 1) -- so any trial must bypass that wrapper and hit Nasdaq Data Link's documented public REST API directly.
challengers.trial_plan: Do not adopt or pin the nasdaq-data-link PyPI package (confirmed stale). If a paid Sharadar/NDL entitlement is ever separately authorized, add a direct-REST arm (plain HTTP against the documented NDL API, no SDK dependency) to the same comparator harness as the Databento trial, scoring: (a) whether SF1's ARQ dimension reproduces as-filed (not restated) fundamentals with filing timestamps that edgartools's XBRL extraction cannot; (b) whether SEP dividend records carry a currency field that alpaca-py's corporate-actions records are missing (native-receipt.json lines 118-130). Pass criterion: both (a) and (b) hold on a small fixed fixture. Overturn: if edgartools's own as-reported XBRL facts already match, or SEP's dividend-currency field is also absent, do not adopt.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none (fundamentals/corporate-actions research question; no execution path reads from Sharadar today)

challengers.name: pandas_market_calendars
challengers.why_better: Not proven better on session semantics -- no executed comparison exists -- but it is a genuinely live, permissively licensed (MIT, independently reconfirmed today: not archived, 999 stars) and actively maintained (v5.4.0 released 2026-05-27, pushed 2026-07-12) direct challenger to exchange_calendars that this layer's own decision text has already flagged since 2026-09-23 as 'should not be mixed' absent a comparison. New motivation this pass found: exchange_calendars is not just a catalog pick, it is imported as a live optional session-open fallback inside the adaptive-paper engine's own sessions.py/runner.py (confirmed by direct code read), so a real session-semantics gap between the two libraries would have actual, if secondary, paper-lane consequences that the layer's existing evidence (one XNYS session, a 104-date check) has never tested against a second library.
challengers.trial_plan: Extend blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__market-data-reference/calendar_check.py (already in the checkout) with a pandas_market_calendars XNYS arm run over the same 2,693 retained sessions and the existing 104-session date check. Pass criterion: 100% agreement with exchange_calendars on session-open/closed status and holiday dates; any disagreement is resolved using sessions.py's own exchange_calendars_agrees() cross-check helper plus a real external source (Alpaca's clock/calendar endpoint) as tiebreak. Overturn: exchange_calendars stays the pin unless pandas_market_calendars is demonstrably more correct on a documented, reproduced mismatch.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: paper acts passed (secondary/fallback path only, not the primary session gate -- see the data-exchange-calendars winner_status note; a session-classification defect here could incorrectly gate or admit a paper order at a session boundary)

challengers.name: sec-api-python (SEC-API.io) -- targeted 13F/insider-trades cross-check only
challengers.why_better: Directly named by this layer's own open_gaps as an 'unindexed alternative'; materially broader scope than edgartools (13F holdings, insider Form 4 trades, enforcement actions, real-time filing streaming). Freshly concrete motivation independently confirmed today: edgartools's own v5.59.1 release notes (2026-09-26) admit edgar_read 'returned no 13F holdings section for any filing' until today's patch -- i.e. the incumbent's 13F path was completely broken until hours before this review, which is exactly the capability sec-api-python is built around.
challengers.trial_plan: On the free tier only (no purchase -- research-only per task rules), pull 13F holdings for one filing already covered by this project's existing SEC fixtures (e.g. an accession from blueprints/us-equities/catalyst-provenance/access-resolution.json) via both the just-patched edgartools v5.59.1 and sec-api-python's free tier, and diff the extracted holdings tables. Pass/overturn: if edgartools v5.59.1's own fix already reproduces sec-api-python's holdings output exactly, no adoption is warranted -- the pin bump alone closes the gap; sec-api-python is adopted only as a conditional cross-check if a real extraction discrepancy survives the patched edgartools.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none (filing-extraction correctness feeds research, not the live paper order path)

researched_candidates.name: alpaca-py
researched_candidates.fit: Incumbent bounded market-data path; confirmed current, not behind upstream. Does not itself close this layer's named gaps: no survivorship-free universe, no dividend-currency field for full cash-unit reconciliation, and no independent establishment of historical point-in-time availability -- these are properties of Alpaca's feed/entitlements, not of the SDK version, and are unaffected by staying current.

researched_candidates.name: edgartools
researched_candidates.fit: Incumbent filing parser. Pin (v5.58.0, 2026-09-11) is now two patch releases behind upstream, both released the day of this check. The delta is filing-section-boundary and 13F-extraction correctness fixes -- real quality improvements to the acquisition path -- but neither closes the layer's named gaps: no as-known historical filing corpus, no dissemination-lag evidence, no licensing/redistribution-rights record for acquired filings.

researched_candidates.name: exchange_calendars
researched_candidates.fit: Incumbent session-semantics library; confirmed current, not behind upstream, with no evidence of pending functional changes being missed. Does not itself close the layer's named gap that native evidence covers only one XNYS session and a 104-date check -- that is a gap in this project's own test coverage of the library's session data, not evidence the library lacks other-venue/extended-hours/halt support upstream.

researched_candidates.name: pandas_market_calendars
researched_candidates.fit: Direct challenger to exchange_calendars for session semantics. Both libraries are now permissively licensed (exchange_calendars Apache-2.0, pandas_market_calendars MIT) and both actively maintained, so the layer's own overturn condition -- compare on representative securities/venues before switching -- is the correct gate. No executed comparison exists yet on venue coverage, extended hours or halts for either candidate.

researched_candidates.name: Massive (formerly Polygon.io) Python client
researched_candidates.fit: This is exactly the comparator arm this layer's own open_gaps names ('a Databento or Massive arm cannot be scored without new code'). Directly read the repo README (rebrand notice) and the pricing page. Confirms the pre-gathered 'Massive' awesome-list entry is current and dated 2026, and resolves what looked like two unrelated repos (massive-com/client-python vs. polygon-io/client-python) into one rebranded product. Redistribution rights for the free tier remain unestablished from what I read, consistent with this layer's own licensing gap.

researched_candidates.name: Databento
researched_candidates.fit: Strongest new-find candidate addressing two named gaps at once: corporate-action completeness (an explicit, dated event taxonomy) and 'licensed, source-identifiable' observations (a paid, documented-provenance dataset vs. scraping-based free feeds). The 6-year point-in-time corporate-actions history is a direct, dated answer to this layer's 'original historical point-in-time availability is not established' gap for corporate actions specifically. A direct fetch of the corporate-actions spec page did not return readable content, so this rests on Databento's own blog/announcement pages rather than a page I read in full myself, and it has not been compared against Alpaca on this layer's own frozen protocol; cost is unverified from what I read.

researched_candidates.name: Norgate Data (norgatedata)
researched_candidates.fit: The most direct available answer to this layer's #1 named gap ('No survivorship-free universe... the Alpaca receipt covers one retrospective AAPL sample'). Norgate explicitly markets survivorship-bias-free coverage including delisted names and historical index constituents -- exactly the universe property Alpaca's current evidence lacks. Access model differs sharply from alpaca-py: it needs a paid subscription and a running Windows desktop updater service as the actual data source, not a pure SDK call, and I found no public source repository to review -- evidence here is vendor/product description and independent quant-blog reviews, not code.

researched_candidates.name: CRSP US Stock Database (Center for Research in Security Prices)
researched_candidates.fit: The academic field's reference standard for exactly the property this layer's requirement, decision text and overturn_when repeatedly name: a survivorship-free universe with permanent identity, delistings and ticker reuse. Not a software library -- access is institutional (typically via a WRDS subscription), so it does not fit an alpaca-py/edgartools 'pip install' pattern, but it is the primary comparison point any survivorship-free claim from Norgate, Sharadar, or a broker feed should ultimately be measured against. I read product/description pages, not underlying data or a full methodology paper, and found no 2026-dated primary confirmation of current update cadence.

researched_candidates.name: Sharadar SEP/SF1 on Nasdaq Data Link
researched_candidates.fit: Closes both the survivorship-free-universe gap and the point-in-time-fundamentals gap in one paid dataset family, with an explicit as-reported dimension that is a direct, quotable answer to 'reject data whose historical availability... is unknown.' Caveat found while checking: the official Python client (nasdaq-data-link, formerly Quandl) has not shipped a new PyPI version since 1.0.4 on 2022-08-29, even though the GitHub repo shows a commit as recently as 2026-09-15 -- the wrapper library's release cadence is stale even if the underlying dataset and repo activity are not.

researched_candidates.name: sec-api-python (SEC-API.io)
researched_candidates.fit: This layer's own open_gaps explicitly names this repo as an 'unindexed alternative' to edgartools, so I checked it directly. It is materially broader in scope than edgartools's filing-parsing focus -- 13F holdings, insider trades, enforcement actions and real-time streaming map onto capabilities this layer's gap list says have 'no native evidence among the adopted candidates.' It sits behind a paid commercial API (typical free-tier query caps apply per the vendor, not independently verified here), so it needs the same licensing/redistribution check as Databento/Massive/Norgate before adoption. Repo activity (last push 2026-04-13, about five months before this check) is thinner than edgartools's near-daily cadence.

researched_candidates.name: OpenBB
researched_candidates.fit: Strongest candidate for this layer's named gap 'no generalized multi-provider comparator exists' -- OpenBB's whole design is a provider-agnostic interface, so it could plausibly host an Alpaca-vs-Databento-vs-Massive comparison without hand-rolled code, unlike the current hard-coded, AAPL-only compare.py. Licensing is a real constraint: OpenBB's own repository license is AGPL-3.0-only (GitHub license field), notably more restrictive than alpaca-py/edgartools/exchange_calendars' permissive licenses, and needs an explicit decision before any OpenBB code (not just its data) ships in this stack.

researched_candidates.name: yfinance
researched_candidates.fit: Free, zero-cost cross-check baseline against Alpaca bars -- useful against this layer's own 'no executed provider comparison' gap as the cheapest possible comparison arm. It is explicitly unofficial with no SLA and no corporate-action-completeness or licensing guarantee, so it cannot itself satisfy the 'licensed, source-identifiable' requirement; its value is strictly as a free sanity-check comparator, not a replacement for alpaca-py.

researched_candidates.name: fedfred
researched_candidates.fit: Addresses this layer's named macro-vintage gap only partially. It is the actively maintained FRED-family client -- unlike the alternative pystlouisfed, whose GitHub repo (TomasKoutek/pystlouisfed) has had no commit since 2024-01-09 and is therefore unmaintained by the 12-month rule despite explicitly claiming ALFRED vintage-data support per its own description. There is a real, unresolved trade-off between 'maintained, no confirmed vintage data' (fedfred) and 'has vintage data, unmaintained' (pystlouisfed) that neither candidate alone closes.

researched_candidates.name: FinanceDatabase
researched_candidates.fit: A candidate for a permanent-identity/universe reference layer, which is adjacent to but distinct from this layer's survivorship-free-history gap: FinanceDatabase is a static symbol/classification catalog (what exists and how it is classified today), not a point-in-time, delisting-aware historical dataset. It complements rather than replaces Norgate/Sharadar/CRSP for the survivorship-free gap specifically.

researched_candidates.name: quantlab (Rossod4)
researched_candidates.fit: This layer's own open_gaps names this repo as an 'unindexed alternative,' and its stated scope -- point-in-time data, SEC EDGAR fundamentals, survivorship measurement -- maps almost exactly onto this layer's top two gaps by description alone. However: 0 stars, no declared license (license field is null), and the description itself says 'in progress.' There is no evidence here beyond the repository's own self-description -- no tagged release, no independent validation, nothing installable under a stated license. This is a repository to watch, not a candidate to compare against Alpaca/Norgate/CRSP/Sharadar today; worth a re-check if it reaches a licensed, tagged release.
